poc_summary: /poc/crl.der is a crafted, properly-signed (RSA-512/SHA256) 200-byte DER X509_CRL whose crlExtensions include an attributeDescriptor extension (NID_attribute_descriptor) encoding an OSSL_ATTRIBUTE_DESCRIPTOR -> OSSL_PRIVILEGE_POLICY_ID -> OSSL_INFO_SYNTAX (POINTER choice) -> OSSL_INFO_SYNTAX_POINTER whose nested OSSL_HASH has algorithmIdentifier set but hashValue (the ASN1_OPT ASN1_BIT_STRING field) deliberately omitted/NULL -- built via the OpenSSL API in a one-off generator program (build_crl.c, not part of the final reproducer) and saved as the PoC input. The reproducer command, identical across all three versions, is the project's own oss-fuzz harness: `/work/fuzz/crl-test /poc/crl.der` (via /poc/run.sh), which exactly mirrors the oss-fuzz fuzz/crl.c path: d2i_X509_CRL -> X509_CRL_print -> X509V3_extensions_print -> X509V3_EXT_print -> dispatch to the attributeDescriptor extension's registered i2r method -> i2r_HASH.
explanation: The intro commit (cccdf41010d0) adds the attributeDescriptor X.509v3 extension support (OSSL_ATTRIBUTE_DESCRIPTOR/OSSL_HASH and i2r_HASH), where i2r_HASH unconditionally dereferenced hash->hashValue->data/length even though hashValue is ASN1_OPT (optional) in the OSSL_HASH ASN.1 template -- so a CRL/certificate whose hashValue is omitted causes a NULL dereference when printed. Reproduced precisely using the project's own oss-fuzz harness (fuzz/crl-test, which is exactly what the reporter used: d2i_X509_CRL + X509_CRL_print) fed the identical crafted, validly-signed CRL DER file across all three versions. post_intro aborts (SIGABRT) with a UBSan 'member access within null pointer of type ASN1_BIT_STRING' report at v3_attrdesc.c:88 inside i2r_HASH, with a call stack running through X509_CRL_print -> X509V3_extensions_print -> X509V3_EXT_print, matching the original issue's own before/after transcript. post_benign (the upstream fix/benign companion), run with the exact same input and command, completes cleanly (exit 0) because the fix adds an explicit `hash->hashValue == NULL` check before the dereference. pre_intro completes cleanly too, but because the entire attributeDescriptor/OSSL_HASH feature (including the vulnerable i2r_HASH) did not exist prior to the intro commit at all -- confirmed separately via a compile-time check showing the relevant types/functions are undeclared in pre_intro's headers -- so the bug is intrinsic to, and wholly introduced by, the intro commit. The same input file and run command were used unmodified across all three versions, satisfying the same-reproducer invariance requirement.

oracle.bug_marker: crypto/x509/v3_attrdesc.c:88:44: runtime error: member access within null pointer of type 'ASN1_BIT_STRING' (aka 'struct asn1_string_st'), stack: i2r_HASH -> i2r_INFO_SYNTAX_POINTER -> i2r_OSSL_INFO_SYNTAX -> i2r_OSSL_PRIVILEGE_POLICY_ID -> i2r_OSSL_ATTRIBUTE_DESCRIPTOR -> X509V3_EXT_print -> X509V3_extensions_print -> X509_CRL_print_ex -> X509_CRL_print -> FuzzerTestOneInput (fuzz/crl.c:32); process SIGABRTs (run_poc reports post_intro: exit=134 crashed=True).
oracle.pre_marker: run_poc(pre_intro): exit=0 crashed=False, output "# /poc/crl.der" with no sanitizer report -- the attributeDescriptor NID/extension type does not exist in pre_intro at all (it and i2r_HASH were introduced atomically by the intro commit), so the unrecognized extension OID is simply not dispatched to any custom i2r routine and the CRL prints without incident.
oracle.benign_marker: run_poc(post_benign): exit=0 crashed=False, output "# /poc/crl.der" with no sanitizer report -- the fix's added `if (hash->hashValue == NULL) return 0;` guard in i2r_HASH prevents the dereference, so the same CRL prints (truncated at the hash value) without crashing.
oracle.description: Behavioral oracle: feed the same crafted, validly-signed CRL DER file (/poc/crl.der, containing an attributeDescriptor extension whose nested Hash.hashValue optional field is omitted) into the project's own oss-fuzz crl-test harness (/work/fuzz/crl-test), identically across pre_intro, post_intro, and post_benign. post_intro must abort with a UBSan null-pointer/member-access report inside i2r_HASH; pre_intro must complete cleanly (the feature/extension type did not exist yet, so it cannot dispatch to the vulnerable code, which is itself confirmed absent via a build-time check); post_benign must complete cleanly because of the added NULL guard.
oracle.target_evidence: Using the actual oss-fuzz crl-test binary (/work/fuzz/crl-test, built as part of each version with the project's configured sanitizers) against the identical crafted CRL file /poc/crl.der in all three versions: pre_intro exits 0 cleanly (feature/API did not exist yet, confirmed separately by a compile-time check that the OSSL_ATTRIBUTE_DESCRIPTOR/OSSL_HASH types and i2d_OSSL_ATTRIBUTE_DESCRIPTOR/OSSL_ATTRIBUTE_DESCRIPTOR_free functions used to build this CRL's extension are entirely absent from pre_intro's headers); post_intro aborts (SIGABRT, exit 134) with a UBSan 'member access within null pointer of type ASN1_BIT_STRING' report at v3_attrdesc.c:88 inside i2r_HASH, with a full call stack showing it is reached through the genuine X509_CRL_print extension-printing path exercised by the oss-fuzz crl fuzzer (matching the issue's own before/after transcript almost verbatim, modulo a small line-number shift from local diffs); post_benign exits 0 cleanly with the same input and command, consistent with the fix's explicit NULL check visible in post_benign's v3_attrdesc.c source (`if (hash->hashValue == NULL) return 0;` immediately before the `print_hex(... hash->hashValue->data ...)` call). This is the project's own upstream fix (24f72a5aaab0) and the same reproduction method (fuzz/crl-test test-case) the OpenSSL maintainers themselves used in the GH-28221 report.
